trial_court: Judicial Magistrate, 1st Class, Patna in Phulwari Sharif P.S. Case no. 264 of 2012
case_name: Arun Kumar Singh & Ors vs State Of Bihar & Anr

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Arun Kumar Singh, Shardanand Singh, Vidyarthi Devi (husband, father, wife)
parties.respondent_defendant: The State of Bihar, Rubi Kumari (wife, opposite party no.2)

facts_of_case: Petitioners' second marriage with opposite party No.2 after death of first wife; opposite party No.2 did not live properly with petitioners to lead conjugal life, leading to cruelty and divorce case filed by petitioners.

legal_principles.principle: Continuance of criminal proceeding involving all family members when FIR does not disclose specific allegation against them will be abuse of the legal and judicial process.
legal_principles.held: It is consistent view of the Hon'ble Supreme Court that continuance of criminal proceeding involving all the family members of husband when FIR does not disclose specific allegation against them will be abuse of the legal and judicial process.
cited_cases: PLJR 2013(1) SCC 10 (Geeta Mehrotra & Anr. Vs. The state of U.P. & Anr.)

legal_principles.principle: Mere casual reference of names of family members in a matrimonial dispute without any allegation of their active involvement is not sufficient to involve them in the proceedings.
legal_principles.held: In the case reported in PLJR 2013(1) SCC 10 (Geeta Mehrotra & Anr. Vs. The state of U.P. & Anr.), the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that mere casual reference of names of family members in a matrimonial dispute without any allegation of their active involvement in the offence is not sufficient to involve them in the proceedings.
cited_cases: PLJR 2013(1) SCC 10 (Geeta Mehrotra & Anr. Vs. The state of U.P. & Anr.)

outcome.final_order: Cognizance taken against petitioners under Section 498A of the I.P.C. and Section ¾ of Dowry Prohibition Act quashed.
